newsitem.title: USA: NYSE Oct 21-25 program trading averages 10.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: NYSE Oct 21-25 program trading averages 10.2 pct.

text.p: New York Stock Exchange said program trading for the week of Oct 21-25 averaged 10.2 percent of its average daily volume of 410.6 million shares, or 41.7 million shares a day.
For the prior week, program trading averaged 11.0 percent of its average daily volume of 434.5 million shares, or 48.0 million shares.
Of the average 41.7 million shares during the week, buy programs accounted for an average 25.0 million shares, while sell programs accounted for an average 16.7 million daily.
In all markets program trading averaged 56.3 million shares a day during the week of Oct 21-25.

Of the five member firms reporting the most program activity on the Big Board, Morgan Stanley, Lehman Brothers and First Boston executed most of their program activity for their own accounts. First Options and Salomon Brothers executed all or more of their program activity for customers, as agent or facilitator.

Between Oct 21 and 25, 25.2 percent of program trading volumed executed by NYSE member firms was related to index arbitrage, while another 18.8 percent involved other derivative product-related strategies.

Program volume executed on the exchange by firms as agent, for non-member customers, amounted to 59.4 percent during Oct 21-25. Program volume executed as principal, for their own accounts, amounted to 37.2 percent of program volume.
Program trading encompasses trading strategies involving the sale or purchase of a basket of at least 15 stocks with a value of $1 million or more the exchange said.
